steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and project-management experience. Review PMI's education and hours-of-project-experience requirements for your background. Granite PM Academy's admissions team can verify your qualifications before enrollment, so you move forward with confidence.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP training course. Attend scheduled sessions from your location in or around Philadelphia at times that fit your work schedule. Our active certified practitioners deliver real-world scenarios and exam-aligned content across the five process groups.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After course completion, submit your PMP application directly to PMI with your education and experience documentation. Pay PMI's exam fee at that time. Granite PM Academy provides clear guidance on the application portal and required supporting materials throughout the process.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Take the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice tests, study guides, and Q&A support—to reinforce your learning. Schedule your exam with PMI's testing partner at a location convenient to you. Our instructors remain available to answer final questions before you sit for the assessment.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After certification, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) throughout the three-year renewal cycle by completing approved training, volunteering, or publishing. Granite PM Academy offers continuing education options to help you meet renewal requirements and stay current in project-management practice.

fq_items.question: Do I need to travel to {city} for this training?
fq_items.answer: No. All of our PMP training is delivered live-virtual via video conference, so {city} professionals attend from wherever they work. No commuting or hotel required.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.

fq_items.question: What is your pass guarantee?
fq_items.answer: If you complete our course and do not pass the PMP exam within 90 days, we provide additional coaching sessions at no additional cost until you pass.

fq_items.question: Is this training PMI-approved?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Granite PM Academy is a PMI Premier Authorized Training Partner (ATP). Our curriculum is aligned to PMI’s current Examination Content Outline and our contact hours are fully accepted by PMI.

fq_items.question: Is PMP certification worth it for Philadelphia project managers?
fq_items.answer: Philadelphia's job market—anchored by Comcast, major health systems, and academic institutions—heavily values structured project governance and capital program delivery. PMP-certified professionals nationally report a median salary premium of approximately $26,000 annually over non-certified peers. While Philadelphia's general project manager salaries range roughly $95,000–$104,000, the credential meaningfully strengthens candidacy for leadership roles in telecom, healthcare IT, and hospital operations where certification is often preferred or required.

fq_items.answer: PMP certification carries particular weight in Philadelphia's dominant sectors: telecommunications and media (Comcast), healthcare systems (Penn Medicine, Jefferson Health, Children's Hospital), higher education (University of Pennsylvania), and insurance (Independence Blue Cross). Hospital capital projects, IT transformation initiatives, and multi-stakeholder corporate programs—common in these sectors—rely on formal project-management rigor that the PMP credential directly addresses.

This format works well for Philadelphia professionals balancing full-time roles at Comcast, health systems, universities, or other major employers, eliminating commute time while maintaining real-time instructor interaction and peer engagement.

However, timing your certification before applying for senior program roles—common in hospital system expansions, digital transformation, and capital planning—maximizes your competitive advantage. Early certification also builds your credential visibility within the local professional network before promotions are posted.
